questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The distance between Sun and Earth is $R$. The duration of year if the distance between Sun and Earth becomes $3 R$ will be:
questions.solution:
Basically 1 year is equal to time period of earth revolution around sun.
So, $T_i=1$ year
Now,
$T^2 \propto R^3\therefore\left(\frac{T_2}{T_1}\right)^2=\left(\frac{R_2}{R_1}\right)^3\Rightarrow T_2=\left(\frac{R_2}{R_1}\right)^{3 / 2} T_1=\left(\frac{3 R}{R}\right)^{3 / 2} \times 1=3 \sqrt{3}$ years.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The kinetic energy of a satellite in its orbit around the earth is E. What should be the kinetic energy of the satellite so as to enable it to escape from the gravitational pull of the earth?
questions.solution:
We know that $v_e=\sqrt{2} v_0$, where $\mathrm{v}_0$ is orbital velocity.
K.E. in the orbit, $E=\frac{1}{2} M v_0{ }^2$
K.E. to escape $E=\frac{1}{2} M v_e^2=\frac{1}{2} M\left(2 v_0{ }^2\right)=\frac{1}{2} M v_0^2 \times 2=2 E$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two identical particles each of mass ' $m$ ' go round a circle of radius $a$ under the action of their mutual gravitational attraction. The angular speed of each particle will be:
questions.solution:
Radius of circle, $\mathrm{r}=\mathrm{a}$
Centrifugal force, $F=m \omega^2 r$
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{Gmm}}{(2 \mathrm{a})^2}=\mathrm{m} \omega^2 \mathrm{a} \\ \\ & \left(\because \mathrm{F}=\frac{\mathrm{G} \mathrm{M} \mathrm{M}_2}{\mathrm{ d}}\right) \\ \end{aligned}$
Here $M_1=m ; M_2=m and d=2 a$
\Rightarrow angular speed, $\omega=\sqrt{\frac{G m}{4 a^3}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two planets $A$ and $B$ of radii $R$ and $1.5 R$ have densities $\rho$ and $\rho / 2$ respectively. The ratio of acceleration due to gravity at the surface of $B$ to A is :
questions.solution:
Acceleration due to gravity,
$\mathrm{g}=\frac{\mathrm{GM}}{\mathrm{R}^2}=\frac{4}{3} \pi \mathrm{G} \rho \mathrm{R}$
$\therefore \frac{g_2}{g_1}=\frac{\rho_2}{\rho_1} \times \frac{R_2}{R_1}=\frac{1}{2} \times 1.5=\frac{3}{4}$

questions.q: What should be the velocity of rotation of earth due to rotation about its own axis so that the weight of a person becomes $\frac{3}{5}$ of the present weight at the equator. Equatorial radius of the earth is $6400 \mathrm{ km}$.
questions.solution:
True weight at equator, $W=m g$ Observed weight at equator,



\mathrmW^{\prime}=$\mathrm{mg}^{\prime}=\frac{3}{5} \mathrm{mg}At equator, latitude $\lambda=0$ Using the formula,



$\begin{array}{l}$\mathrm{mg}^{$\prime}=$\mathrm{mg}-\mathrm{mR}$ \omega^{2} $\cos ^{2} \lambda\\\frac{3}{5}\mathrm{mg}=\mathrm{mg}-\mathrm{mR}$ \omega^{2} $\cos ^{2}0=\mathrm{mg}-\mathrm{mR}$ \omega^{2}\\

\Rightarrow $\mathrm{mR}$ \omega^{2}=$\mathrm{mg}-\frac{3}{5}\mathrm{mg}=\frac{2}{5}\mathrm{mg}$\\

\therefore \quad \omega=$\left(\frac{2}{5} \frac{\mathrm{g}}{\mathrm{R}}\right)^{1 / 2}$\\

=$\left(\frac{2 \times 9.8}{5 \times 6.4 \times 10^{6}}\right)^{1 / 2}$=7.8 \times10^{-4} $\mathrm{rad}$/ $\mathrm{s}$

\end{array}

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Kepler's third law states that square of period of revolution (T) of a planet around the sun, is proportional to third power of average distance $\mathrm{r}$ between sun and planet i.e. $\mathrmT^{2}=\mathrm{Kr}^{3}$ here $\mathrm{K}$ is constant. If the masses of sun and planet are $\mathrm{M}$ and $\mathrm{m}$ respectively then as per Newton's law of gravitation force of attraction between them is $\mathrm{F}=\frac{\mathrm{GMm}}{\mathrmr^{2}}$, here $\mathrm{G}$ is gravitational constant. The relation between $\mathrm{G}$ and $\mathrm{K}$ is described as
questions.solution: As we know, orbital speed, $V_{\text{orb }}=\sqrt{\frac{\text{ GM }}{\text{ r }}}$ Time period $\mathrm{T}=\frac{2 \pi \mathrm{r}}{\mathrm{v}_{\text{orb }}}=\frac{2 \pi \mathrm{r}}{\sqrt{\mathrm{GM}}} \sqrt{\mathrm{r}}$ Squarring both sides, $\mathrm{T}^{2}=\left(\frac{2 \pi \mathrm{r} \sqrt{\mathrm{r}}}{\sqrt{\mathrm{GM}}}\right)^{2}=\frac{4 \pi^{2}}{\mathrm{GM}} \cdot \mathrm{r}^{3}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\mathrm{T}^{2}}{\mathrm{r}^{3}}=\frac{4 \pi^{2}}{\mathrm{GM}}=\mathrm{K} \Rightarrow \mathrm{GMK}=4 \pi^{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An artificial satellite is moving in a circular orbit around the earth with a speed equal to half the magnitude of the escape velocity from the earth. The height $(h)$ of the satellite above the earth's surface is (Take radius of earth as $R_{e}$ )
questions.solution: The escape velocity from earth is given by $v_{e}=\sqrt{2 \mathrm{ g} R_{e}} \ldots$ (i) The orbital velocity of a satellite revolving around earth is given by v_{0}=$\frac{\sqrt{\mathrm{G} M_{e}}}{\left(R_{e}+h\right)}$ where, $M_{e}=$ mass of earth, $R_{e}=$ radius of earth, $h=$ height of satellite from surface of earth. By the relation $\mathrm{G} M_{e}=\mathrm{g} R_e^{2}\text{ So, } \quad$ v_{0}=$\frac{\sqrt{g R_e^{2}}}{\left(R_{e}+h\right)} \ldots$ Dividing equation (i) by (ii), we get $\frac{v_{e}}{v_{0}}=\frac{\sqrt{2\left(R_{e}+h\right)}}{\left(R_{e}\right)}$ Given, $v_{0}=\frac{v_{e}}{2}\frac{2 v_{e}}{v_{e}}=\frac{\sqrt{2\left(R_{e}+h\right)}}{R_{e}}$ Squaring on both side, we get 4=$\frac{2\left(R_{e}+h\right)}{R_{e}}$ or $R_{e}+h=2 R_{e} \quad$ i.e., $h=R_{e}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Geo-stationary satellite is one which
options: remains stationary at a fixed height from the earth's surface
revolves like other satellites but in the opposite direction of earth's rotation
revolves round the earth at a suitable height with same angular velocity and in the same direction as earth does about its own axis
questions.solution:
Geo-stationary satellites are also called synchronous satellite. They always remain about the same path on equater, i.e., it has a period of exactly one day $(86400 \mathrm{sec})$ So orbit radius $\left(\mathrm{T}=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{\mathrmr^{3}}{\mathrm{GM}}}\right)$ comes out
to be $42400 \mathrm{~km}$, which is nearly equal to the circumference of earth. So height of Geostationary satellite from the earth

$\text{ surface is }$42,400-6400=36,000 $\mathrm{~km} \text{ . }$
